connections.why: Atomic masses underpin the mole calculations used in every reaction
Electronic structure explains an element's position and behaviour
Whether atoms gain, lose or share electrons depends on their group
Metallic bonding and electron loss underlie the reactivity series
Crude oil is separated into fractions because it is a mixture
Mole ratios let you calculate amounts in neutralisation reactions
Reactivity determines how metals react with acids to form salts
More reactive metals release more energy in displacement reactions
Energy profiles and temperature both control reaction rate
Industrial processes optimise rate and equilibrium yield
Covalent bonding explains the structure of organic molecules
Polymers and fuels are key products of the chemical industry
Manufacture and disposal of chemicals affect air and resources
Burning hydrocarbons releases the gases that change the atmosphere
Acidic gases dissolve in water to affect oceans and rainfall
Group trends predict how vigorously metals and non-metals react
